title: M5Unified #446: PCF8563 begin() clears Timer_control TE (virtual-device validation)

execution.environment: macOS arm64 build host; ESP-IDF v6.0.2; Device Service dial profile (M5Dial, qemu-esp32s3, PCF8563 I2C model)

checks.detail: issue #446 is open, authored by atgcgcta in Japanese, with 0 comments before this work; no prior m5agent reply

PCF8563_Class::begin() at src/utility/rtc/PCF8563_Class.inl:22 unconditionally writes 0x0E=0x03 (TE=0, TD=0b11). M5.begin() calls Rtc.begin() at src/M5Unified.inl:2874 and only afterwards checks cfg.disable_rtc_irq at 2883-2884; disabling the IRQ through config cannot prevent the earlier write

M5Dial QEMU: timer pre-armed as 0x0E=0x82; after M5.begin(cfg.disable_rtc_irq=false) the register reads 0x03; setTimerIRQ(1000) restores 0x82 (C2=0x09, CNT=0x01); calling Rtc.begin() again returns it to 0x03; re-arming restores 0x82
with the one-line 0x0E,0x03 -> 0x00,0x00 replacement, the pre-armed 0x82 survives M5.begin(cfg.disable_rtc_irq=false) and a subsequent Rtc.begin(); C2/CNT still show the timer armed
ESP-IDF v6.0.2 build for esp32s3 succeeded; merged image 490 KiB; an independent rebuild of the unmodified source reproduced artifact SHA256 e11ccbe3... byte-for-byte
no CoreInk hardware available; the physical board, its PCF8563 circuit and the INT pin were not observed
the Device Service inventory has no CoreInk profile; M5Dial was used because it exposes the same PCF8563 driver path and a validated RTC model
INT pin waveform, long-term period drift, and current consumption after the TD change were not measured
the default cfg.disable_rtc_irq=true path was not executed on the virtual device; source inspection shows disableIRQ() writes 0x0E=0x00 at PCF8563_Class.inl:281
no upstream push, PR, or patch submission; the proposal is recorded only as a local patch for the maintainer

notes: Reply language is Japanese to match the issue title and body; one comment only, no close, no push, no changes to the upstream repository.
The issue is a chip-driver behavior, so the M5Dial virtual board exercises the same PCF8563_Class code path even though CoreInk is not modeled.
The proposed patch keeps the existing two-write initialization pattern and leaves the default disable_rtc_irq=true behavior to disableIRQ().
